<sup>1</sup> שרפאתיו ע"י רחיצת הירדן whom I cured by bathing in the Jordan. Ib. שהסרתי … ע"י רחיצת וכ' whom I saved from drowning through the bathing of Pharaoh’s daughter. Ib. גחזי שלקה ע"י ר' Gehazi who was punished on the occasion of (Naaman’s) bathing; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="T00513">
<head-word>רָחֵל</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> f. (b. h.)
<pos> pr. n. f.</pos>
<italic>Rachel</italic>, 1) wife of Jacob.</definition>
<notes>, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition />

<sense>

<entry id="T00514">
<head-word>רָחֵל</head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>ewe, sheep</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Bekh. III, 1 ר' בת שתים וכ' if an ewe gives birth in her second year of age, the issue belongs to the priest with certainty. Ib. 20
<sup>a</sup>. Tosef. Ḥull. X, 1 כלאיים מן הר' וכ' a hybrid of an ewe and a kid is subject to the law concerning the first of the fleece (Deut. XVIII, 4); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. רְחֵלֹות, רְחֵלִים, רְחֵלִין, רְחֵי'</plural-form>. Ib. 4 השוטף רְחֵלָיו if one washes his lambs (and wool comes out). Ib.; Ḥull. XI, 2 חמש ר' גוזזות וכ' five lambs yielding wool of the weight of &c. Ib. 137
<sup>b</sup> דקא מתני ליה לבריה רחלים taught his son (the Mishnah l. c.) using 
<italic>r’ḥelim</italic> (according to Biblical usage); א"ל אתנייה רחלות said he to him, teach him 
<italic>r’ḥeloth</italic> (in accordance with later usage). Bekh. V, 3 זכר של ר', v. זָכָר. Sabb. V, 2; 4; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="T00515">
<head-word>רְחֵלָא</head-word>

<sup>c</sup> top; v. רַחֲמָנָא. Keth. 63
<sup>a</sup> (prov., with ref. to Akiba’s daughter, betrothed to Ben ʿAzzai for many years, and alluding to Rachel, the name of Akiba’s wife, v. רָחֵל I) ר' בתר ר' אזלא וכ' ewe follows ewe, as the mother acts, so does the daughter; a. e.—
<plural-form>Pl. רְחֵלִין, רְחֵלֵי, רְחֵי', רַחְל'</plural-form>. Targ. Gen. XXXII, 15 (14) (O. ed. Berl. רַחְלי). Targ. Deut. XIV, 4 (O. ed. Berl. רַחְלִין); a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="T00516">
<head-word>רָחַם</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>to love</italic>.</definition>
<notes /></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>רִיחֵם</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> (with (with על) 
<italic>to have compassion on, pity; to befriend</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 33
<sup>a</sup> כל מי … אסור לרַחֵם עליו you must not befriend him who has no sense (ref. to Is. XXVII, 11). Sabb. 151
<sup>b</sup> כל המְרַחֵם … מְרַחֲמִין עליו וכ' he who shows mercy to creatures (men), will be shown mercy in heaven (ref. to Deut. XIII, 18), v. רַחֲמָן. Ab. Zar. 18
<sup>a</sup> מן השמים יְרַחֵמוּ heaven will have mercy (protect me); Nidd. 45
<sup>a</sup>. Sot. VIII, 1 יְרַחֲמוּ עליכם they will have mercy on you (spare your lives); a. fr.—Trnsf. 
<italic>to give suck to a strange animal</italic>. Bekh. 24
<sup>a</sup> אינה מְרַחֶמֶת אלא וכ' no dam gives suck to a stranger, unless she has had a child of her own. Ib. מרחמת אע"פ וכ' she may give suck, even if she has never given birth.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to stimulate the maternal instinct</italic> (v. 
<xref rid="T00516">רֶחֶם</xref>) of an animal after confinement by inserting a lump of salt into the womb.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Sabb. XV (XVI), 2 מְרַחֲמִין היינו בהמה טהורה ביו"ט ed. Zuck. (Var. על בהמה) we (in my father’s house) used to stimulate &c. on a Holy Day; Sabb. 128
<sup>b</sup> על בהמה; Y. ib. XVIII, end, 16
<sup>c</sup> על הבהמה.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְרַחֵם</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to have pity</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 9
<sup>24</sup> אם נופלים אנו … מִתְרַחֵם עלינו אין אנו מִתְרַחֲמִים עליו if we fall into David’s hands, he will have pity on us, but if David fall into our hands, we shall have no pity on him; Y. Sot. I, 17
<sup>b</sup> bot. הוא מרחם … אנו מרחמין).</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="T00517">
<head-word>רְחֵם</head-word>
<head-word>רְחֵים</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to love</italic> (h. אהב).</definition>
<notes> Targ. Gen. XXII, 2. Ib. XXXVII, 3. Targ. O. Deut. VI, 5. Targ. Prov. IV, 6 (ed. Wil. רָחֲמָהּ 
<italic>Pa.</italic>); a. fr.—Midr. Till. to Ps. XVIII, 2 (expl. ארחמך, ib.) רַחֲמִית יתך וכ' I love thee (ref. to Targ. Deut. l. c.); Yalk. ib. 671 רַחְמָאִי יתך. Y. Ber. IX, 14
<sup>b</sup> bot. (R. Akiba speaking to his pupils before his death) רְחִמְתֵּיה בכל לבי ורחמתיה וכ' I loved him with all my heart, and I loved him with all I possessed, but how to love him with all my soul (life) I could not understand, and now &c. Sabb. 23
<sup>b</sup> דרָחֵים רבנן וכ' he who loves scholars shall have children that are scholars. Y. ib. XIV, 14
<sup>d</sup> bot. חד בר נש ר' אתתא וכ' a man fell in love with a woman … and grew dangerously ill; Y. Ab. Zar. II, 40
<sup>d</sup> bot. Lev. R. s. 25 שמעית דמלכא רַחְמָא וכ' I heard that the king loves figs; Koh. R. to II, 20 רחים; ib. רחימא; ib. רחמיה (corr. acc.). Y. Ab. Zar. II, 41
<sup>a</sup> bot. דהוות רַחְמָא מצוותא who loved to be charitable; Y. Ter. VIII, 45
<sup>c</sup> bot. הוו רחמנא וכ' (corr. acc.). Keth. 105
<sup>b</sup> אם מִרְחַם כולהו רַחְמוּ לי וכ' if there is love (among them), they all love me &c., v. סְנֵי. Snh. 89
<sup>b</sup> תרוייהו רַחֲמִינִי להו I love both of them (Isaac und Ishmael); a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (with על) 
<italic>to have compassion on, pity</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Ps. CIII, 13. Targ. Prov. XXVIII, 13; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>רַחֵם</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to love</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Gen. XXIX, 32 (O. ed. Vien. 
<italic>Pe.</italic>). Targ. Y. Deut. VI, 5; a. e.—Keth. l. c. האי … דמְרַחְמִין ליה וכ' if the people of a place love a teacher, it is not because he is a good man, but because he does not reprove them on heavenly matters (for neglect of religious duties). Y. Ter. VIII, 45
<sup>c</sup> אילולי דאתון מרחמין שמועתא וכ' but for your loving traditions (you would not ask such questions); is it not a Mishnah?; Y. Ab. Zar. II, 41
<sup>a</sup> רחמין; a. e.—Trnsf. 
<italic>to give suck</italic> (v. preced.). Bekh. 24
<sup>a</sup> or shall we say, דידה מְרַחְמָא דלא וכ' a dam gives suck to her own young, but not to a stranger. Ib. דילמא רַחוּמֵי רחים perhaps this is a case when one gives suck to a stranger (although having a child of her own); v. שְׁבַק.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (with על) 
<italic>to compassionate, pity</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Jer. XXXI, 19. Targ. O. Num. VI, 25 וירחם עלך ed. Lisb. (oth. ed. ויר' יתך; in ed. Berl. untranslated). Targ. Deut. VII, 2; a. fr.—Macc. 23
<sup>b</sup> מדהא מְרַחַמְתָּא והא לא מרחמתא (Solomon found out which was the true mother of the living child,) because the one showed compassion, and the other did not. Y. Taan. II, 65
<sup>b</sup> אמרין … מִתְרַחֵם עלינן לינן מְרַחְמִין וכ' the men of Niniveh said, if thou wilt have no mercy on us, we shall have no mercy on them (the beasts and the children); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Ithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִתְרחֵם, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Ithpe.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִתְרְחֵם</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be loved, beloved</italic>.</definition>
<notes>. Targ. Prov. XV, 9.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (with על) 
<italic>to be pitied, be shown mercy</italic>.</definition>
<notes>. Targ. Y. Ex. XXXIII, 19. Targ. Gen. XLIII, 29. Targ. Hos. XIV, 4; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be moved to mercy, have pity</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Jer. XXXI, 18 (19) מתרחם ed. Lag. (oth. ed. מתנחם; h. text נחמתי).—Y. Taan. l. c., v. supra; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="T00518">
<head-word>רָחָם</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>raḥam</italic>, name of an unclean bird, 
<italic>giereagle</italic> or 
<italic>vulture</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥull. 63
<sup>a</sup> ר' זו שרקרק ולמה … ר' כיון שבא ר' וכ' 
<italic>raḥam</italic> (Lev. XI, 18) is the 
<italic>sh’raḳraḳ</italic>, and why is it called 
<italic>raḥam</italic> (love)? Because when the 
<italic>r.</italic> comes, mercy comes upon the world (it betokens rain).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>orifice of the matrix; womb</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Bath. 16
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. רַחְמָהּ צר, v. אַיָּלָה. Num. R. s. 10
<sup>5</sup> קבלה הר' וכ' (fem.) the womb conceived &c. Ḥull. 70
<sup>a</sup> כותלי בית הר' the sides of the womb; a. fr.—Gen. R. s. 37; Yalk. Ps. 869 (ref. to Ps. CX, 3) מרַחְמוֹ של אולם שחרתיך לי from the womb of the world (sunrise, east) did I choose thee for me.—
<plural-form>Pl. רְחָמִים</plural-form>. Ḥull. l. c. Ber. 32

<italic>friend</italic>.</definition>

<sup>b</sup> דרָחְמֵיה קמצא whose friend’s name was Ḳamtsa. Gen. R. s. 96 בריה דרָחְמִיךְ thy friend’s son, v. טְעַן II. Y. Shebi. IX, 39
<sup>a</sup> top בגין דלית … רחם whereas these people (we) have no friend; a. e.—
<plural-form>Pl. רַחֲמִין, רַחְמֵי, רָ'</plural-form>. Targ. Prov. VIII, 36. Targ. Ps. XXXVIII, 12 Ms. (ed. רְחִי'). Targ. O. Gen. XXVI, 26 רַחְמוֹהִי ed. Berl. (oth. ed. מרח'); a. e.—Y. Shebi. l. c. חמי לך תלתא ר' וכ' choose thee three friends &c. Yalk. Gen. 115, v. רְחִים II. Sabb. 32
<sup>a</sup> Ar. (ed. מרחמי); a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>a</sup>, v. רַחְמָנוּתָא.—Trnsf. 
<italic>maternal instinct, giving suck to a strange animal</italic> (v. רָחַם, a. רְחַם). Bekh. 24
<sup>a</sup> חיישינן לר' we consider the possibility of her giving suck to a strange animal.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="T00525">
<head-word>רַחֲמֵיּ</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />

<entry id="T00526">
<head-word>רַחֲמִים</head-word>
<pos> m. pl.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> רָחַם)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>love, mercy</italic>; (sub. בקשת) 
<italic>prayer</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 7
<sup>a</sup> שיכבשו רַחֲמַי את כעסי וכ' that my mercy may conquer my anger &c., v. גָּלַל. Ib. שיכבשו רַחֲמֶיךָ וכ' that thy mercy &c. Ib. 10
<sup>a</sup>, sq. אל ימנע עצמו מן הר' must not despair of mercy (cease to pray), v. מָנַע. Ib. 55
<sup>a</sup> שלשה צריכים ר' three things must be prayed for. Ab. II, 3, v. קֶבַע. Lev. R. s. 2, end הריני עמו בר' וכ' I shall be in grace with him, and he will receive me in repentance. Num. R. s. 20, beg. כל הנביאים היו במדת ר' על וכ' all the (Israelitish) prophets were benevolently disposed towards Israel and towards the nations; a. v. fr.—בקש ר' to ask for mercy, 
<italic>to pray</italic>. Macc. 11
<sup>a</sup> שהיה להן לבקש ר' על וכ' it was their duty to pray for their generation &c. Sabb. 67
<sup>a</sup> ורבים יבקשו עליו ר' and the people will pray for him. Ib. 151
<sup>b</sup> לעולם … ר' על מידה זו וכ' man must always pray concerning this condition (poverty), for if he does not come to it, his son will &c.; a. fr., v. בָּקַשׁ.—מדת הר', v. דִּין II. כסא ר', v. כִּסֵּא.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>b</sup> בעא ר' וכ' he prayed, and it returned to its place; a. fr.; v.

<entry id="T00528">
<head-word>רַחֲמָן</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (preced.) 
<italic>merciful, compassionate, sympathetic</italic>; הר' 
<italic>the Merciful, God</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. B. Kam. IX, 30 (ref. to Deut. XIII, 18) כל זמן שאתה ר' הר' וכ' if thou art merciful, the Merciful will have mercy on thee. Kidd. 81
<sup>b</sup> הר' יצילנו וכ' the Lord save us from evil inclinations. Midr. Till. to Ps. CIII, 13 כר' שבאבות like the most merciful of the patriarchs (Abraham). B. Bath. 145
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Prov. XV, 15) זה ר' this means the sympathetic man. Snh. 39
<sup>a</sup> אם ר' הוא … אם ר' מלא רחמים הוא וכ' if he (the human king) is merciful, he puts half of them (the rebels) to death; if he is most merciful, he chastises the prominent &c.; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. רַחֲמָנִים, רַחֲמָנִין</plural-form>. Yeb. 79
<sup>a</sup> שלשה … הר' וכ' this nation (Israel) is known by three characteristic features, they are merciful, chaste, charitable; Y. Kidd. IV, 65
<sup>c</sup>; Midr. Till. to Ps. XVII. Pes. 113
<sup>b</sup> שלשה חייהן … הר' וכ' there are three persons whose lives are no lives, the sympathetic, the hot-tempered, and the delicate. M. Kat. 27
<sup>b</sup> (to those mourning to excess) אמר הקב"ה אי אתם ר' בו יותר ממני (Ms. M. omits בו) the Lord says, you do not bear him more love than I do?; a. e.—
<italic>Fem.</italic> (b. h.) רַחֲמָנִית. Tanḥ. Vayetsé 8 אמר לה הקב"ה את ר' וכ' the Lord said to her (Leah), thou art compassionate, I will also have compassion on her (Rachel).—
<plural-form>Pl. רַחֲמָנִיּוֹת</plural-form>. Meg. 14
<sup>b</sup> מפני שהנשים ר' הן because women are compassionate. Ex. R. s. 2, beg. מדותיו … ר' הן the dealings and dispositions of the Lord are full of love; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="T00529">
<head-word>רַחֲמָן</head-word>
<head-word>רַחֲמָנָא</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same.</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> Targ. Y. Lev. XXII, 28 (not רחמין, v. infra). Targ. Y. Num. XII, 13; a. e.—Esp. רחמנא 
<italic>the Merciful, God</italic>. Targ. Ps. CXII, 4. Targ. Ex. XXXIV, 6; a. e.—Y. Ber. V, 9
<sup>c</sup> top (ref. to Lev. XXII, 28) אילין דמתרגמין … כמא דאנא ר' … כך תהוון רחמנין וכ' those who in the interpretation of this verse say, my people, as I am merciful in heaven, so shall you be merciful: cow or ewe &c.; Y. Meg. IV, 75
<sup>c</sup> top דאנן רחמין (corr. acc.).—Y. Kidd. I, 61
<sup>b</sup> בריך ר' דלית וכ' blessed be the Lord that I have neither father nor mother (because it is so difficult to do one’s duty by one’s parents); Y. Peah I, 15
<sup>c</sup> bot. Taan. 9
<sup>b</sup> ר' ליצלן וכ' the Lord save us &c., v. כִּיסּוּפָא; a. fr.—Trnsf. 
<italic>the Word of God, Scripture, the Law</italic>. B. Mets. 3
<sup>a</sup> דרמיא ר' שבועה וכ' the Law imposes an oath upon him. Ib.
<sup>b</sup> ואמר ר' רמי וכ' and the Law says, impose an oath upon him. Ker. 7
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Lev. XXI, 12) שמן … קרייה ר' וכ' the Scripture calls it oil of ordination (sacred) to intimate, that it does not lose its sacred character even after being put on his head; a. v. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. רַחֲמָנִין</plural-form>. Targ. Y. Lev. l. c.—Y. Ber. l. c.; Y. Meg. l. c.; a. e.—[Y. Ter. VIII, 45
<sup>c</sup> bot. הוו רחמנא, v. רְחֵם.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="T00530">
<head-word>רַחֲמָנוּת</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (preced.) 
<italic>love, mercifulness, compassion</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Succ. 14
<sup>a</sup> מדת ר' divine mercy, opp. אכזריות. Keth. 50
<sup>b</sup> יודע אני … אלא מידת ר' I know that thou decidest so not as a matter of justice but as a matter of humanity. Gen. R. s. 56 ונופלות … מרַחֲמָנוּתוֹ של אבא and tears of paternal love fell upon Isaac’s eyes; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="T00535">
<head-word>רָחַץ</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>to bathe, wash</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 122
<sup>a</sup> מותר לִרְחוֹץ בה מיד it is permitted to bathe in it immediately (after the exit of the Sabbath); ib. 151
<sup>a</sup>; Makhsh. II, 5 רוֹחֵץ מיד. Ber. 15
<sup>a</sup> מי שאין … לרחוץ ידיו (Ms. M. ליטול) he that has no water with which to wash his hands (before prayer). Tosef. Keth. VII, 6 ורוֹחֶצֶת במרחץ עם כל אדם a woman that bathes in a bath-house with all kind of people (loses her jointure). Y. ib. VII, 31
<sup>b</sup> bot. (as a case for divorce) הדירה שלא תִרְחֲצִי וכ' if he bound her by a vow (saying), thou shalt not bathe in a bath-house; a. fr.—Part. pass. רָחוּץ. Zeb. 17
<sup>b</sup> שלא רְחוּץ ידים וכ' not having washed his hands and feet (before a sacred function); Tosef. Men. I, 9. Ib. 12 שלא רחוץ, Var. ולא רָחְצוּ.</notes></sense></senses>
<pgbrk id="pg1469" />
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִרְחִיץ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> same, same, 
<italic>to wash, cleanse</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ib. 10 משפשף ומַרְחִיץ he rubs and washes (hands and feet). Ber. l. c. (ref. to Ps. XXVI, 6) דכתיב אֶרְחַץ ולא אַרְחִיץ (v. Ms. M., Rabb. D. S. a. l.) it is written 
<italic>erḥats</italic> (I bathe), and not 
<italic>arḥits</italic> (I cleanse), i.e. washing of hands as a symbolical act is equal to immersion. Y. Keth. V, 30
<sup>a</sup> bot. ומַרְחֶצֶת לו וכ' she must bathe his feet (personally attend to his foot-bath). Yalk. Cant. 988 שמַרְחִיצִין את ישראל וכ' who cleanse Israel from sins; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to cause to bathe</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 13
<sup>2</sup> עתיד … ולהַרְחִיצָם בנחלי חלב the Lord shall cause them to drink …, and to bathe in rivers of milk. Sabb. l. c.; Makhsh. l. c. מרחץ המרחצת בשבת a bath-house that allows bathing (is heated and open) on the Sabbath. Y. Ber. II, 4
<sup>c</sup> bot. מרחץ ואע"פ שאינה מרחצת a bath-house, even if it is not in use.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>רִיחֵץ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to cleanse</italic>.</definition>
<notes>—Part. pass. מְרוּחָץ; 
<plural-form>pl. מְרוּחָצִין</plural-form>. Cant. R. to IV, 4 שהיו כולן מר' מן העונות they were all cleansed of their sins.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִרְחַץ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be cleansed</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yalk. Cant. l. c. שהטיף … ונִרְחֲצוּ מעונותיהם the Lord dropped dew upon them, and they were cleansed of their sins.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="T00536">
<head-word>רְחֵץ</head-word>
<head-word>רְחֵיץ</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (with על, or ב־) 
<italic>to lean on; to trust; to be safe</italic>.</definition>

<sup>a</sup> רְחִיצַיָּא אנן we are sure (cmp. מובטח, v. בָּטַח). Snh. 7
<sup>a</sup> גברא דרחיצנא עליה וכ' the man in whom I trusted lifted up his club &c.; a. e.</notes></sense></senses>

<binyan-form>אִתְרַחֵיץ, </binyan-form>

<xref rid="T00349">רוּחְצָן</xref>). Targ. Jer. XLIX, 4; a. fr.—B. Bath. 91
<sup>b</sup> דמודי … דמִתְרְחִיץ עליהון וכ' he who assents to them (pretends to share their errors) falls into their hand; he who confides in them,—what is his is theirs. Y. Sabb. II, 5
<sup>b</sup> לא תִתְרְחֵץ על צלותי rely not on my prayer. Cant. R. to VII, 2 בגין דאִיתְרְחִיצוּ ביה because they trusted in him; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<entry id="T00538">
<head-word>רָחַק</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>to be distant, far, removed</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y’lamd. to Num. X, 29, quot. in Ar. (ref. to Ps. LXXIII, 27) מי שרוֹחֵק הק"בה וכ' (ed. Koh. שׁמִתְרַחֵק) he who keeps away from the Lord, so as not to repent. Sifré Num. 131 כרְחוֹק מזרח וכ' as far as the east is removed from the west; a. e.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>רִחֵק, רִיחֵק</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to remove; to alienate; to reject, expel; to loathe</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Kam. 24
<sup>a</sup> top, a. e. ר' נגיחותיו if the ox did his gorings in intervals (of three days), opp. קירב. Ib. רִיחֲקָה ראיותיה, v. רְאִיָּה. Yalk. Ps. 809 (ref. to Ps. l. c.) זה … שׁרִחֲקוּ את הקץ this alludes to Balaam and his associates, who put far off the end (the day of judgment, Num. XXIV, 17), opp. קרבו. Ber. 60
<sup>b</sup> ורַחֲקֵנִי מאדם רע וכ' keep me far from a bad man and a bad associate. Eduy. V, 7 מעשיך יקרבוך ומעשיך יְרַחֲקוּךָ thy own doings will bring thee near (win thee friends), and thy own doings will alienate thee. Ib. VIII, 7 לרַחֵק, v. קָרֵב; a. fr.—Part. pass. מְרוּחָק; 
<plural-form>pl. מְרוּחָקִים, מְרוּחָקִין</plural-form>. Ib. המר' בזרוע, v. קָרֵב. Ber. 63
<sup>b</sup> שלא היה מר' וכ' which was only twelve miles off.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִרְחִיק</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> same.</definition>
<notes> Sifré Num. 94 מַרְחִיקִים, v. קָרֵב. B. Bath. II, 5 מַרְחִיקִין את הסולם וכ' (neighbors) must keep a ladder removed from the (neighbor’s) dove-cote four cubits. Ib. 4 אלא אם כן ה' ממנו וכ' unless he places (the wall) at a distance of four cubits. Ib. 18
<sup>b</sup> על המזיק להַרְחִיק את עצמו it is the duty of him who causes the damage to remove himself; (oth. opin.) על הניזק להרחיק וכ' he who is injured must remove himself. Ber. I, 1 כדי להרחיק וכ' in order to keep men away (prevent them) from sin. Snh. 103
<sup>b</sup> שהִרְחִיקָה וכ', v. לְגִימָה. Ib. מַרְחֶקֶת וכ' estranges those who are near (related) &c.; a. fr.—2) 
<italic>to keep aloof, stay away</italic>. Ab. I, 7 הַרְחֵק משכן רע keep aloof from a bad neighbor; a. e.—[Y. Ber. I, 2
<sup>d</sup> bot. והרחיק על פתחו וכ', read: והִרְתִּיק, v. רָתַק.]</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְרַחֵק, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִתְרַחֵק</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to remove one’s self; to become a stranger</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yeb. 109
<sup>a</sup> לעולם ידבק … ויִתְרַחֵק וכ' man should always cling to three things, and keep aloof from three things. Snh. III, 4 קרוב ונ', v. קָרוֹב. Ber. 34
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Is. LVII, 19) שהיה קרוב … ונ' וכ' who came near committing a sin, and withdrew himself from it. Y’lamd. l. c., v. supra; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="T00539">

<sense>

<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> rocks are mentioned, and the same rule applies to sand, so there (Sabb. IV, sand is mentioned, and rocks are implied; Yeb. 31
<sup>b</sup>; B. Mets. 31
<sup>a</sup>.</definition>
<notes> Ab. ch. VI נקרא ר' he is called a friend (of God); a. fr.—Esp. 
<italic>lover, paramour</italic>, contrad. to בעל. Ex. R. s. 32 (ref. to Jer. III, 20) מאישה לא נאמר אלא מֵרֵעָהּ מה אשה … בבעלה אלא ברֵעָהּ וכ' it does not say, ‘to her husband’, but ‘to her lover’, as a woman cannot rebel against her husband, but can deny her lover, because there is no marriage contract between them, so said the Lord to Israel, לא
